questions.text: What is the main goal of model quantization?
options: Increase the number of parameters in the model
Reduce model size and inference cost by using lower-precision number formats
Add more training data to improve accuracy
Convert the model from Python to C++
questions.explanation: Quantization maps weights from high-precision formats (FP32/FP16) to lower-precision ones (INT8, INT4), shrinking model size and speeding up inference with minimal quality loss.

questions.text: What is the key difference between PTQ and QAT?
options: PTQ requires more GPU memory than QAT
QAT can only be applied to small models
PTQ trains the model from scratch while QAT does not
PTQ quantizes after training is complete, while QAT simulates quantization during training
questions.explanation: Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) converts an already-trained model, while Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) injects fake quantization nodes during training so the model learns to compensate for precision loss.

questions.text: What is the GGUF format primarily used for?
options: Storing training datasets in a compressed format
Defining model architecture in YAML
Packaging quantized models for efficient local CPU/GPU inference
Encrypting model weights for secure deployment
questions.explanation: GGUF (GPT-Generated Unified Format) is a single-file format used by llama.cpp and similar tools to store quantized model weights with metadata for efficient local inference.

questions.text: Which of the following are true about INT4 quantization compared to INT8?Select all that apply
options: INT4 always produces better quality outputs than INT8
INT4 uses half the bits per weight compared to INT8, yielding smaller models
INT4 requires no calibration data
INT4 typically incurs more quality degradation than INT8
questions.explanation: INT4 halves the bits per weight compared to INT8, making models smaller and faster, but the coarser representation typically causes more accuracy loss. Careful calibration helps mitigate this.

questions.text: What is a common deployment strategy for serving quantized LLMs to many users?
options: Running quantized models behind an API with batched inference on GPU servers
Emailing the model weights to each user individually
Running the full FP32 model on a single CPU
Storing the model exclusively in browser localStorage
questions.explanation: Quantized models are commonly served through API endpoints that batch requests and use GPU acceleration, providing low latency and cost-efficient inference at scale.
